title: Stakeholders
log: 2026-10-27T01:00:11Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No existing point teaches stakeholders and their conflicting interests; the closest points, on customers, suppliers and competitors and on business in the economy, cover related but different ideas.

draft.title: Stakeholders
card: A stakeholder is any person or group with an interest in a business, or who is affected by what it does. They do not have to own it.
Common stakeholders are owners, employees, customers, suppliers, the government and the community. Each wants something different from the business.

Owners want profit. Employees want fair pay and safe work. Customers want good products at fair prices. Suppliers want to be paid on time. The government wants tax paid and laws followed. The community wants jobs and a clean local area.
Stakeholder interests often conflict. For example, higher wages for employees can mean lower profit for owners. Managers must weigh these interests when they make decisions.
draft.remember: A stakeholder is anyone with an interest in a business, and their wants often clash.

a.q: Which of these people is a stakeholder in a bakery in Orange?
opts: A supplier who sells the bakery its flour
Only the person who owns the bakery
Only the staff who bake the bread
A shopper in another state who has never heard of it
a.why: A stakeholder is anyone with an interest in the business, and a supplier depends on its orders. Owners are stakeholders too, but they are not the only ones, so limiting the group to owners is wrong.
a.clue: Stakeholders do not need to own the business.

b.q: Dan owns a printing firm in Geelong. He cuts staff overtime pay to lift profit. Which two stakeholder groups have interests that conflict here?
b.why: Owners want higher profit, while employees want fair pay, so cutting overtime helps one and hurts the other. Customers and suppliers are not directly affected by this decision, so they are less tempting as the conflict.
b.clue: Think about who gains from lower wage costs and who loses.

a.best: A supplier who sells the bakery its flour
